applies_why: This judge text resolves a collision involving the challenger's own footed covenant-origin chain by relying on a single sentence's own words, the situation K-C governs.
quote: the sentence's own words state the source of what is in the womb
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: never verse by verse — one reading: a judge may still use the challenged sentence's own words as support; the other: K-C requires the whole collision to be weighed chain against chain by footing and bars relying on an isolated verse's own words.
why: The judge acknowledges the challenger's analogy is footed but then resolves the collision by citing the challenged sentence's own words, rather than weighing the challenger's chain against the link by footing as K-C requires.
